summary: Final report MV-2022-176 for Orvessant Biosciences Pty Ltd: Five-isoform DDI screen on 40 compounds (Piperidyl benzamide). Study summary table on page 1; full compound tables, methods, controls and deviations follow.

title_block.title: OB11 GPCR antagonists: five-isoform CYP inhibition at screening concentration
title_block.subtitle: Final Report
lines: Study lead: Dr M. Larkin, DMPK Study Director

blocks.p: 40 compounds from the Orvessant piperidyl benzamide series 11 were tested for Orvessant Biosciences Pty Ltd in the Five-isoform DDI screen. Testing started on July 25, 2022 and results were reported on August 10, 2022. All accepted runs met matrix acceptance criteria. Inhibition above 50% at 10 µM was most frequent for CYP2C9.
To rank the test article set for Five-isoform DDI screen liability so that Orvessant Biosciences Pty Ltd could choose analogues for progression.

40 compounds were received as 10 mM DMSO solutions in one accession lot on July 25, 2022 and logged against M22/BIO/04063. Identity and concentration were taken as supplied by the client. Stocks were stored at -20 °C and thawed once for testing.

Pooled human liver microsomes (0.1 mg/mL protein) were incubated with each compound at 10 µM and an isoform-selective probe substrate at approximately Km, in duplicate, for 10 minutes at 37 °C after NADPH addition. Metabolite formation is measured by LC-MS/MS against vehicle (0.1% DMSO) incubations; the lower limit of quantitation of each metabolite is at least 20-fold below the vehicle signal.

Positive controls are run as 7-point concentration responses on every run. Furafylline and ticlopidine (mechanism-based inhibitors) are preincubated with microsomes and NADPH for 15 minutes before probe addition. A run is accepted when each control IC50 falls within 0.5-2 times the laboratory historical mean. Results are reported as mean percent inhibition relative to vehicle; values above 50% at 10 µM are flagged, and small negative values indicate no inhibition.

Inhibition above 50% at 10 µM was most frequent for CYP2C9. In total {{PRJ0006:cyp.n_any_gt50}} compounds inhibited at least one isoform by more than 50% at 10 µM (CYP3A4: {{PRJ0006:cyp.n_gt50_CYP3A4}}; CYP2D6: {{PRJ0006:cyp.n_gt50_CYP2D6}}; CYP2C19: {{PRJ0006:cyp.n_gt50_CYP2C19}}; CYP2C9: {{PRJ0006:cyp.n_gt50_CYP2C9}}; CYP1A2: {{PRJ0006:cyp.n_gt50_CYP1A2}}). All control IC50s were within 0.5-2 times the historical mean (ketoconazole {{PRJ0006:cyp.control_CYP3A4_uM}} µM against a historical mean of {{PRJ0006:cyp.hist_CYP3A4_uM}} µM).
No deviations from the study plan.
Inhibition above 50% at 10 µM was most frequent for CYP2C9. Values are in vitro and do not by themselves predict clinical risk; free exposure estimates are needed for that assessment.
Recommended next steps: run concentration responses for compounds flagged on CYP2C9 and any other isoform above 50%.
Raw data, assay worksheets and instrument files are retained for 5 years under M22/BIO/04063.
